hints.content: Therefore, we can set up equivalent proportions and solve for $k$.

$\dfrac{\red{k}}{\blue{6}} = \dfrac{\red{13}}{\blue{26}}$

 Note: As each corresponding $\dfrac{\red{\text{side}}}{\blue{\text{side}}}$ proportion is equivalent, you could use the other sides (i.e., $\dfrac{\red{k}}{\blue{6}} = \dfrac{\red{12}}{\blue{24}}$)

Reduce the proportion on the right hand side.

 $\dfrac{\red{k}}{\blue{6}} = \cancel{\dfrac{\red{13}}{\blue{26}}}{\green{\dfrac{1}{2}}}$

Multiply each side by $6$ and simplify.

 $\cancel{6} \times \dfrac{\red{k}}{\cancel{\blue{6}}} = \green{\dfrac{1}{2}} \times 6$
